key_catalyst: Brent crude above $100/bbl after Iran rejected a ceasefire and Houthis attacked Saudi tankers, combined with new 10-12.5% tariffs on ~60 countries pushing September Fed hike odds to 80%
reasoning: Three independent bearish shocks are stacking simultaneously: Brent breaking above $100 (up from ~$90 on 07-20, ~$95 on 07-22, ~$96 on 07-23) after Iran rejected a ceasefire, brand-new 10-12.5% tariffs on ~60 trading partners, and a September hike probability spiking to 80% — while the Alphabet/Tesla AI-capex ROI sell-off from 07-23 (QQQ -1.90%) is still unresolved with Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Apple all reporting next week. The pre-market response of only -0.30% is far too shallow relative to the described severity, which mirrors 07-20 when QQQ shrugged off the oil/semis warnings (+0.10%) before the theme reasserted itself. Intel's Q2 beat is a genuine positive but is a single-name cushion against a macro shock that hits index-wide duration.
